subject.title: Bug: Orphaned TaskFlows in `waiting` status permanently block agent heartbeats (requests-in-flight deadlock)

question: What TaskFlow wait-abandonment contract should OpenClaw support for managed flows that remain in `waiting` after callback loss, gateway restart, or unreachable external wait metadata?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose this because `waiting` is a durable plugin-managed state with no current deadline field, and the previous blanket-timeout PR showed the compatibility risk.

options.title: Add explicit wait deadlines
options.body: Introduce controller-visible deadline or orphan metadata, expire only flows that opt into or prove abandonment, and run the recovery from the gateway/runtime owner path.

options.title: Keep audit/manual repair only
options.body: Document `stale_waiting` as an operator maintenance signal and avoid automatic terminalization until plugin owners define deadlines.

options.title: Pause for live diagnosis
options.body: Hold implementation until a live gateway reproduction identifies whether TaskFlow state, pending final delivery, active reply runs, or session lanes are the lasting busy resource.

recommendation.title: Add explicit wait deadlines
recommendation.body: Introduce controller-visible deadline or orphan metadata, expire only flows that opt into or prove abandonment, and run the recovery from the gateway/runtime owner path.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly tied to recent TaskFlow audit/maintenance hardening and likely to route the ownership/API decision.
